question.problem: Consider the equation $2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})+3=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ and ${x}_{5}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})+3 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}) & =-3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}) & =-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}) & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x}{2} & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & \frac{5x}{2} & =\frac{7\pi }{6}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+4n\pi  & \, & \, & 5x & =\frac{7\pi }{3}+4n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{4n\pi }{5} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{7\pi }{15}+\frac{4n\pi }{5} \\ x & =\frac{(12n+5)\pi }{15} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(12n+7)\pi }{15}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{7\pi }{15}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{15}$  and $x=\frac{19\pi }{15}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{29\pi }{15}$  and $x=\frac{31\pi }{15}.$ We reject the solution $\frac{31\pi }{15}$ since it lies outside the domain of interest.

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},{x}_{5}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{3},\,\frac{7\pi }{15},\,\frac{17\pi }{15},\,\frac{19\pi }{15},\,\frac{29\pi }{15}.
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{17\pi }{15}=\frac{17{\pi }^{2}}{45}.
$$
